messages.content: You check whether the evidence collected so far is enough to answer a question about a scientific paper. Say sufficient only if, for EVERY sub-question, some evidence item contains the specific fact, number or picture that answers it -- not merely the same topic. If sufficient, give for each sub-question the id of that item (E1, E2, ...) and copy the answering fact in a few words. Otherwise list the numbers of the sub-questions still uncovered and say in a few words what is missing.

Question: What are the three main components of the Action Search model architecture?
Sub-questions:
1. [figure] What are the three main components of the Action Search model architecture?
Evidence:
E1 [figure, Figure 3, page 7] (image attached): Fig. 3: Our model harnesses the temporal context from its current location and the history of what it has observed to predict the next search location in the video. At each step, (i) a visual encoder transforms the visual observation ex- tracted from the model’s current temporal location to a representative feature vector; (ii) an LSTM consumes this feature vector plus the state and temporal location produced in the previous step; (iii) the LSTM outputs its updated state and the next search location; (iv) the model moves to the new temporal location.

answers.fact: The three main components are: (i) a visual encoder, (ii) an LSTM, and (iii) the LSTM's output.
